title: Serving runtime weekly update - kernel / KV cache / batching (2026-10-28)
content:
Date: 2026-10-28
Author: Aisha Patel
Purpose: Weekly sync notes for kernel optimizations, KV cache changes, and batching improvements. Quick status for leads and SRE handoff.

Attendees:
- Aisha (owner)
- Daniel (kernels)
- Riley (KV + cache)
- Marco (batching + perf)
- Priya (SRE / infra)

TL;DR:
- Kernel work: merged vectorized attention patch to mainline, landed 1.8-2.1x speedup on short-seq inference for several model families. Follow-up: microkernel tuning + autotune job in CI next week (SRV-812).
- KV cache: rolled out partial prefix eviction prototype to canary; reduced memory pressure by ~22% on 64k-prefix workloads, some edge-case correctness failures observed (SRV-799).
- Batching: adaptive batcher improvement reduced tail latency for bursty traffic by ~12% at 95th percentile; still planning a change to dynamic batch-timeout logic (PR 512).

Highlights / Wins:
- Kernel vectorization merged (PR 508). Benchmarks on g5.2x showed tokens/sec increase: 1.8x for Llama-2-13B w/seq=128, 2.1x for 7B optimized path. Peak GPU utilization improved ~10pp.
- Autotune harness prototype ran against 10 kernel configs; the harness identified 3 non-obvious kernel parameter sets that outperform default on A100.
- KV cache prototype on canary (us-west-2, dedicated pool) dropped OOM incidents in one customer test by 60% for long-conversation tests.

Kernel work (Daniel):
- Done: Merged vectorized attention, added new fused softmax kernel, added safety checks for FP16 edge cases.
- In progress: Microkernel tiling change (branch: mk-tiling-2026) to reduce L1 cache misses. Aiming to land by 2026-11-03.
- Risks: Autotune results vary by sequence length distribution; need stable CI jobs to run varying seq profiles. Ticket: SRV-812.
- Action items:
  - Add sequence-length-weighted autotune runs to perf CI (Daniel + Marco).
  - Add telemetry tags so we can correlate kernel variant -> observed latency in prod (Priya).

KV cache (Riley):
- Done: Partial prefix eviction implemented, canaryed on 3 nodes. Eviction strategy: LRU-ish with prefix-weight heuristics.
- Observed: Memory reduction ~22% on synthetic long-dialog traces (~64k tokens). However, 3 flaky failures where cache invalidation race produced stale KV reads on rapid rollback scenarios. Root cause looks like a delayed compact path interacting with async evict.
- Next steps:
  - Hotfix: enforce compact-path barrier for rolling upgrades (short-term, by 2026-10-30).
  - Longer term: redesign eviction opportunistically during idle cycles + ensure strict epoch-based invalidation. Design doc: Confluence:SRV-KV-Design-2026.
- Related artifacts: JIRA SRV-799 (eviction correctness), perf traces in linked GCS bucket (see Confluence).

Batching (Marco):
- Done: Deployed adaptive-batcher v2 to staging and canary. Observed 95p latency reduction of ~12% under bursty request patterns (simulated mobile traffic).
- Work remaining: Tune dynamic batch timeout thresholds by region (APAC vs NA profiles differ significantly). PR 512 implements region-aware defaults but needs a config toggle.
- Micro-optimizations: moved certain serialization steps off hot path, saved ~0.6ms per request.
- Action items:
  - Config flag for region-aware batch policy (Marco).
  - Run 48-hour A/B test to validate user-visible latency under real traffic (Priya to schedule).

SRE / infra notes (Priya):
- Canary rollouts: widened canary to additional 5 nodes after kernel merge. No new OOMs, one CPU spike correlated with a background autotune job - capped autotune CPU to 10% in canary.
- Observability gaps: we need finer-grained KV cache metrics (evict count, stale-read rate). Priya to add dashboard tiles and alerts for SRV-799 and SRV-812.
- Incident readiness: drafted rollback playbook for KV cache regressions; will rehearse during next chaos test.

Standup snippets / daily log highlights:
- 2026-10-26: Found non-deterministic failure in cache compact (Riley) - reproduced with race harness.
- 2026-10-27: Kernel vectorization CI flaked on one config (A100-40gb) due to memory alignment; fixed and re-ran.
- 2026-10-28: Batcher timeout tuning produced a small regression for very low qps; rolled back that config in canary and tracking.

Metrics / Benchmarks (summary):
- Kernel vectorized path: +80-110% tokens/sec on short sequences (7B/13B).
- KV cache memory use: -22% on 64k synthetic traces; steady-state for typical 2-5k prefix workloads unchanged.
- Batching P95 latency: -12% under bursty workload; P50 unchanged.

Open issues / blockers:
- SRV-799: cache stale-read failures on rollbacks - high priority.
- SRV-812: autotune variance - need to harden harness and add seq-aware profiles.
- Config management for region-aware batching needs product signoff (blocking larger canary expansion).

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Daniel: land microkernel tiling + CI autotune profile (due 2026-11-03).
- Riley: hotfix barrier for compact path, run race harness across canary (due 2026-10-30).
- Marco: add region-aware batch config flag + open PR for config toggle (due 2026-11-02).
- Priya: create KV cache dashboard tiles and schedule 48h A/B canary (due 2026-11-01).
- Aisha: coordinate customer impact comms if SRV-799 shows up on dedicated pools (ongoing).

Notes / context / references:
- See Confluence:SRV-KV-Design-2026 for design sketches and trade-offs.
- Perf artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/serving-runtime/2026-10-kernel-vectorized/ (bench CSVs).
- Related PRs: 508 (kernel vectorize), 512 (adaptive-batcher), 520 (kv eviction prototype).

Parking lot / future improvements:
- Explore hybrid on-GPU/host KV cache spilling to reduce OOMs for 100k+ token sessions.
- Investigate ML-guided eviction policies for long-tail customer behaviors.

If anything should be added to next week's agenda: deeper review of autotune CI costs (compute/time), formal runbook for KV rollback scenario, and batching config defaults per region.

-- end of weekly update --
